meta_description: Fulfillment is throughput economics: pick rates, dock scheduling, labor allocation and inventory truth.

blocks.x: The contract behind Warehousing & Fulfillment: signed baseline in week two, working slice by week eight, industrialized controls by week twelve, and evidence flowing to your control owner throughout.
Before proposing anything, we map the context Warehousing & Fulfillment will run in — regulators, decision cadence, existing contracts — because the design that ignores context fails at the gate.

blocks.x: The reference pattern behind Warehousing & Fulfillment is boring on purpose: contracts at every boundary, an owner per component, and evidence captured where the work happens. Boring architecture is what survives contact with an audit.
